metadata.remarks:
Identity Core defines the foundational capability that establishes what constitutes an identity within the institution. It provides authoritative identity definition, uniqueness, attribution, and namespace consistency. This capability underpins all other identity patterns.

Governance and Responsibility Anchor:
This pattern is the authoritative anchor for SSPPs, standards, procedures, guidelines, and assurance related to institutional identity definition. Controls are scoped to sub‑capabilities to enable precise assurance while preserving pattern‑level governance.

components.title: Identity Authority
components.description: Authoritative sources of truth responsible for asserting identity existence and core attributes.

implemented-requirements.remarks: Manage identities for organizational users, services, and non-human actors.
Define and govern the enterprise identity architecture.

components.title: Identity Namespace
components.description: Namespaces and identifier schemes ensuring identities are non‑ambiguous.

implemented-requirements.remarks: Ensure identities are uniquely identifiable prior to authentication or access.

components.title: Identity Uniqueness
components.description: Ensures each identity corresponds to a single subject and prevents duplication or collision.

implemented-requirements.remarks: Prevent identity duplication and ensure one‑to‑one subject mapping.

components.title: Identity Attribution
components.description: Ensures actions can be attributed to a defined identity to support accountability.

implemented-requirements.remarks: Generate audit records to support attribution of identity actions.
Access control policies rely on authoritative identity attribution.
